title_liktai: ၽိုၼ်ဢဝ်ၼၢင်း
title_english: Song of Welcoming the Bride (Traditional Wedding Ballad)
informant: Late Chaw Sa Myat Chowlik & Nang Mya Chowlik
description: Ceremonial song chanted at the door threshold of the groom's household in Powaimukh when welcoming the bride into her new family. Includes offerings of betel leaves, silver coins, and sacred blessing cotton threads (saai1 phuk4 mɯ1).
cultural_context: The song is performed in alternating antiphonal verses by senior women of both lineages, ensuring ancestral blessings (phi5 yaa3) and peace in the household.

cultural_context: Rice pounding is a major communal activity before festivals (Sangken, Poy Lu Phraa). Singing in synchronized meter ensures energy and collective joy during arduous physical labor.

title_english: Song of the Sangken Water Festival (Tai New Year)
description: Celebratory song sung during Sangken (the Tai Buddhist Water Festival in mid-April). Villagers sprinkle consecrated scented water on the Buddha image, venerable monks, and one another to cleanse ill fortune and welcome the New Year.
cultural_context: Sangken is the most important cultural festival of the Tai Khamyang. It marks the transition of the sun from Pisces to Aries and strengthens community solidarity across all generations.

description: Lyrical dialogue ballad (Kham Soi Yoi / Cholim) exchanged poetically between young men (bao1) and maidens (sao1), invoking nature allegories, the blooming of wild forest orchids, and deep affection.
cultural_context: Preserves the classical rhythmic poetry of Southwestern Tai, with internal rhymes, assonance, and metaphorical language representing the peaks of the Patkai and the crystal waters of the streams.
